must_fix: C005 (confirmed): the co-emulation field in the step-8 header block offers 'signal-level | transaction-based | unknown' (line 258), but no step ever instructs the reader to write into it — and the exact token 'transaction-based' appears nowhere else in the file. Every other mention of the same concept, including the slot definition (line 53), the explanation in step 2 (line 148), and both Gotchas mentions (lines 301, 303), uses 'transaction-level' instead. A reader following the prose will naturally write 'transaction-level', silently mismatching the declared enum. Fix by renaming the enum value to 'transaction-level' throughout, and add an explicit instruction (e.g. in step 2) to record the Emulator and co-emulation mode slot's answer into this field using that exact spelling.

Step 3's hard-stop sweep (line 154) is scoped only to 'the testbench tree from step 2' and never sweeps the design file set that step 2 already separated out, even though 'timing constructs' (specify/$setuphold/$sdf_annotate) and 'real-number and analog modelling' (real/shortreal/wreal) are common design-side (gate-level/IP/AMS-wrapper) constructs, not testbench constructs. As written, a design-side hard stop that would fail the emulator compile can score clean through this audit. Either add a design-side sweep for these two rows or state explicitly that RTL-side synthesizability is out of scope and deferred entirely to the infra owner's compile (per the step-8 handoff).
technical_errors: Step 3's hard-stop sweep is scoped only to 'the testbench tree from step 2' (line 154, 8 Greps), but two of its own eight rows target constructs that live predominantly in DESIGN-side files, not the testbench: 'timing constructs' (specify, $setuphold, $sdf_annotate, line 163) are near-universally embedded inside gate-level/IP models rather than testbench code, and 'real-number and analog modelling' (real, shortreal, wreal, line 164) is at least as often a design-side AMS behavioural wrapper as a host-side model. Step 2 already separates the design file set out (line 141-142) but step 3 never sweeps it — a genuine hard stop rooted in a design-side IP or gate model would never be found, and the audit would score a test as portable when the emulator compiler would in fact reject it.

The report block's 'checkers' field carries an 'unknown' enum value (line 274) and the Human Verification section requires it be used honestly ('checkers say unknown wherever the budget did not settle them, rather than defaulting to the flattering value', line 347), but step 6 itself (lines 214-230) never states when 'unknown' applies — unlike step 5, which explicitly says 'unknown is a legitimate answer when two Greps do not settle it. Write it.' (line 210) for tb-coupling. A reader following step 6 alone has no instruction for when to write checkers: unknown.
verb_honesty: Clean. Every step stays inside Read/Grep/Glob plus arithmetic on already-read numbers. Step 4 is explicitly titled 'arithmetic, not reading' and says 'This step opens nothing' (line 176) — no tool call implied. Step 8's handoffs are phrased correctly per the rules: 'ask the emulation infra owner to compile the current design file set and give you the path of the compile report' (lines 287-288), 'ask them for the cycles per second a short run actually reached and the path that run wrote to' (line 289), 'ask the DV lead for the per-test time report' (line 291) — the agent never itself compiles, measures a rate, or submits a job; it only reads/greps and then asks a human for the artifact. No bare Run/Execute/Merge/Compute verb applied to the agent anywhere in the 8 procedure steps.
hallucination_risks: Line 143-144: 'One 60-line Read at the top-level filelist records the design's top instance name, which step 3 needs.' Filelists (.f files) conventionally enumerate source paths; they do not generally carry hierarchy/instance-name information unless the house convention happens to embed a -top style directive in the same file. This is exactly the kind of house-specific fact rule 2 says must be a [[FILL:]] slot, but it is stated as plain fact, is not covered by the cited 'Filelist convention' shared fact (which only covers nesting and relative-path resolution, per _shared/team-profile.md line 68), and has no slot of its own. Step 3's back-door reach-in row then depends entirely on this unverified assumption ('the top instance name from step 2, followed by a dot', line 161) with no fallback stated if the filelist does not carry it.

Step 1 (line 98) invents a specific, unhedged-beyond-'roughly' threshold of 1500 rows as the point where the strategy switches from a single bounded Read to Grep-then-windowed-Read. Lower-severity than the filelist claim, but it is a specific number presented as a general rule rather than tied to any team fact or FILL slot.
budget_violations: Rule 7 (line 109-111) permits only 'at most four' narrowing calls total for the eight-pattern sweep in step 3 when a Grep exceeds ~200 hits. In a real testbench tree of the scale this skill assumes ('thousands of files', line 88), several of the eight patterns are individually likely to exceed 200 hits on their own — the delay/wait operator and the 'top instance name + dot' back-door pattern (line 161) in particular are exactly the kind of pattern that returns hundreds of hits in any sizeable UVM environment. If more than four of the eight rows need narrowing, the stated cap is insufficient and the ledger arithmetic in rule 6 (which assumes at most 4 narrowing calls) no longer holds.

Step 1 (line 124) says to 'Read it in windows' (plural) for the regression summary, while the budget (rule 3, line 97) allots only 'one bounded Read' for that same step. If the summary genuinely needs multiple windowed Read calls to cover 'thousands of rows' (line 88), the stated per-step Read allotment undercounts what step 1 actually needs; the rest of the ledger arithmetic (rule 6, 'about sixteen windowed Reads') is otherwise internally consistent (2+2+12=16 Reads, 3+12+24=39 Greps, 2 Globs) so this is the one place the totals may not actually cover what the prose describes.
review.open_twice: Yes, most likely. This is one of the stronger drafts in the batch: the retrieval-budget ledger is internally consistent almost everywhere (2 Globs, ~39-40 Greps, 16 Reads add up correctly across rules 3-5), every declared slot is genuinely consumed somewhere in the procedure, sibling routing in 'When to use something else' points to real, existing skills with an honest division of labor, and verb honesty is maintained rigorously throughout — every emulator action is correctly pushed to a named handoff rather than performed by the agent. The two must-fix items (the dead/mismatched co-emulation enum value, and the testbench-only hard-stop sweep missing design-side constructs) are real and would cost a senior engineer some trust on first read, but they are narrow, fixable gaps rather than the kind of pervasive hallucination or shelfware-inducing verb dishonesty that sinks a draft outright.

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean, the budget arithmetic is exact (2 Globs / 47 Greps / 18 Reads reconciles across rules 3-5 and every step fits), all ten slots and four profile facts are spent, and role/level are emulation-engineer/intermediate. But step 4 — the arithmetic the entire ranking is built on — has two load-bearing defects. (a) Every payoff number needs simulated time converted to cycles ("convert using the design's clock period"), and the clock period is not a slot, not a profile fact, and not readable inside the budget; because the Runtime columns slot only ever collects wall clock and simulated time, this is the universal path, not the conditional branch step 4 frames it as, so every headroom and cap rests on an invented number that the Human-verification checklist passes. (b) "Divide the row's simulated time by the simulation rate: that is what the run would have taken had it been nothing but design work" is false given the Rate pair slot's own wording ("the design cycles per second our regression ACHIEVES in simulation") — an achieved end-to-end rate already contains the regression's average host work, so the residual is excess host work relative to average and the crossing cap is systematically over-estimated; for any test at or below average host overhead the gap collapses, the cap goes unknown, and step 7 falls back to raw headroom, which is precisely the optimistic ranking the skill's own "wrong answer" paragraph describes. Third, smaller: the intro, step 7's port-after-rework criterion, step 8's routing prose and Done-when all require a per-row owner, but the emitted candidate block has no `owner` field even though `owner` is a registered shape in _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md with exactly those semantics.
remaining: Step 4 has no source for the clock period. Both rates are cycles/second and the only time datum collected is simulated time (Runtime columns slot), so 'convert using the design's clock period' is required on every run, not conditionally. The period is not a slot, not in _shared/team-profile.md, and has no budget allowance to be read. Fold it into the Rate pair slot (or add a slot) so no payoff number rests on an invented frequency; the current Human-verification bullet ('every payoff number traces to a summary column Runtime columns says exists') passes a ranking built on a guessed clock.

Step 4's host-share baseline uses the wrong rate. Rate pair defines the simulation number as the rate 'our regression ACHIEVES', which already includes the regression's average host testbench work, so cycles / that rate is NOT 'what the run would have taken had it been nothing but design work'. The residual is host work in excess of the regression average; the derived host share is understated and the crossing cap (1 / host share) is systematically optimistic. Worked case: true design-only 10k cyc/s, regression-achieved 5k cyc/s, emulator 1M cyc/s, 100M-cycle test with a genuine 50% host share -> gap is zero, cap goes unknown, step 7 key 3 ranks on headroom 200 for a test whose real ceiling is 2x. Either state that the figure is host work relative to the regression average and that the cap is an upper bound only, or require a design-only rate in the slot.

The candidate block emits no `owner` field, though the intro promises 'who owns that rework', step 7 grants port-after-rework only 'when the rework is named and owned', step 8 routes each rework line through the profile's area-to-owner map with the blank-plus-candidates rule, and Done-when requires naming the person per porting row. `owner` is a registered shape in _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md with exactly that meaning ('The name from the profile's area-to-owner map, or blank plus candidates') - add it to the per-candidate block.
new_problems: Step 4's 'The host share, from the other half of Rate pair' bullet — the slot table's justification note ('Both halves of Rate pair are spent') marks this as material added to consume an unspent slot half, and it consumed it with an end-to-end achieved rate used as if it were a design-only rate. The optimism it introduces lands on the exact ranking key (step 7 key 3) that the skill's 'wrong answer' paragraph warns about.

The clock-period conversion in step 4 is written as a conditional ('If the summary records simulated time rather than cycles') while the Runtime columns slot makes it the only path — the conditional framing hides a fact with no source behind an 'if' that is always true.
